(AP Photo) The fallout from Australia's explosive Sandpapergate controversy has taken another turn, with broadcaster Fox Cricket taking former openers Usman Khawaja and David Warner off its commentary roster as fresh revelations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal continue to rock Australian cricket. Fox Sports managing director Steve Crawley confirmed that both commentators would be rested from broadcasts over the next few weeks, acknowledging that the continuing controversy had made it increasingly difficult for them to concentrate on their broadcasting responsibilities. No return date has been announced. Watch Inside India's dressing room coffee culture ft. Devdutt Padikkal “In light of recent events, both Usman and Davey will be rested from our broadcasts over the next few weeks,’’ Crawley told CODE Sports. “While we always support all members of our commentary team and welcome a diversity of views, which is a feature of our summer of cricket, we also understand the pressure they are under to respond to every new comment," he added. “We think it is increasingly difficult to focus on the game while the situation continues to unfold and think it is unfair on both commentators to put them in that position," he said. “Our focus remains on providing our viewers with the best broadcast of Australia’s summer of cricket. We will continue to monitor the situation," he concluded. Khawaja, Bancroft revelations reignite Sandpapergate
 The controversy has resurfaced following revelations in Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr, and subsequent comments from Cameron Bancroft suggesting that knowledge of the ball-tampering plan extended beyond the three players who were initially sanctioned. Bancroft was caught using sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball during the Cape Town Test against South Africa in March 2018. The scandal resulted in suspensions for then captain Steve Smith, vice-captain Warner and Bancroft, triggering one of the biggest crises in Australian cricket. In his autobiography, Khawaja questioned the extent of knowledge within the Australian dressing room about the plan. Bancroft subsequently added fuel to the controversy through a column in The West Australian, alleging that the wider squad was aware of what was happening and that discussions about generating reverse swing had involved members of the bowling group, including Join conversation

 Pat Cummins . Bancroft described Cummins' recent press conference as the 'final straw' that prompted him to break his silence. Cummins rejects allegations as CA backs captain
 Cummins strongly rejected the allegations when questioned about them in Sydney, describing the suggestion that the entire team knew about the plan as "complete and utter nonsense". The renewed controversy has put Australia's Test captain under scrutiny, with questions emerging over his position amid the fresh claims. Cricket Australia, however, has backed Cummins to continue as skipper, issuing a statement of support. Australia face England in the first of five T20 Internationals at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Saturday, before opening their home Test summer against New Zealand at Perth Stadium on December 9.
